scope: Topology-resolved point-to-point label cache, KFI, and KEYGL5 OEM controls

grounding.evidence: native direct LABEL CLEAR, KFIGET/KFISET, CLEAREDLT and FactoryDefault captures retained in decode_to_pci.jsonl, kfi.jsonl and transport regressions
grounding.finding: The direct captures establish every CAL payload, confirmation requirement, selector order, acknowledgement tag, KFI reply shape and native command result envelope.

grounding.evidence: routed RECALL, STORE, Unlock and IDENTIFY implementation vectors and tests in cbus-transport::pci::programming
grounding.finding: The retained point-to-point source-route contract establishes one-to-six bridges, PCI confirmation allocation, and strict Reply Network first-bridge/remaining-hop/remote-unit correlation.

claimed_behavior: LABEL CLEAR preserves the native confirmation-only result while sending exactly once through a database-resolved one-to-six-bridge route.

KFIGET sends three selector writes and one IDENTIFY exactly once; KFISET sends four writes exactly once. Each phase requires its exact PCI confirmation and route/unit/parameter-correlated Reply Network receipt.
CLEAREDLT and FactoryDefault require exact PCI confirmation plus route/unit/tag-correlated Reply Network acknowledgement.
Remote operations do not invalidate the configured-network dynamic-label observation ring.
acceptance: Transport tests pin the exact one- and six-bridge wire bytes, direct and foreign-route isolation, selector ordering, acknowledgement tags, KFI decoding and invalid-route pre-I/O refusal.
Service tests pin topology resolution, remote KEYGL5 classification, native response envelopes and configured-network cache isolation.
limits: This is a composition of separately retained native direct command payloads and routed point-to-point contracts; no exact native C-Gate capture of these combined remote commands is claimed.
Confirmation and acknowledgements prove accepted transport receipts, not cache erasure, rendered labels, reset effects, address retention, reboot behavior or persistence.
Live physical bridge and remote KEYGL5 acceptance remains outstanding.
